title: The Faithful Bridge
premise: In 1911, Felix Ishikawa, a young woman passing as an apprentice clockmaker in her late father's workshop, is summoned to repair the harbor observatory's master clock. There she discovers a sealed letter hidden in the clock's case — evidence that her family's shipping firm has been named in an embezzlement plot orchestrated by the port magistrate, who intends to make the Ishikawas the scapegoats. With the incriminating ship manifest due to sail on the morning tide and three checkpoints between her and the harbor master's office, Felix must decide whether loyalty to her family's name matters more than the truth of what they've done. She smuggles the letter through the night, exposes the magistrate at dawn, and chooses to rebuild the family business honestly rather than preserve its reputation — letting the old clock, and the old lies, stop for good.
about_author: Lior Nakamura is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing port ledgers from the early twentieth century. Their fiction explores how families inherit not only trades but silences.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Felix Ishikawa, disguised as her late father's male apprentice to keep the workshop's license, repairs a merchant's watch while her mother frets over debts. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: quiet pride shadowed by the fear of being found out.

chapters.title: Summons at Dusk
chapters.summary: A clerk delivers an official summons to repair the observatory's master clock before the equinox inspection. Felix's uncle Tadao warns her to refuse, but the fee would save them. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dread braided with ambition.

chapters.title: The Room Where Time Is Kept
chapters.summary: Felix climbs the observatory tower and meets Inspector Voss, the magistrate's man, who watches her too closely as she works. The great clock's mechanism is sabotaged, not merely worn. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Case Conceals
chapters.summary: Cleaning the clock's housing, Felix finds a sealed letter and a duplicate ship manifest naming Ishikawa & Sons in a cargo fraud. The handwriting is her father's. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: vertigo — the ground of memory giving way.

chapters.title: Her Father's Hand
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Felix learning the trade at her father's bench, his lessons about honest weights. Now she rereads those memories hunting for signs of the crime. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief interrogating love.

chapters.title: Uncle Tadao's Silence
chapters.summary: Felix confronts Tadao, who admits he knew of irregular shipments but swore an oath to her dying father. He begs her to burn the letter. POV: Tadao. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Invitation
chapters.summary: Magistrate Corven receives Felix courteously, offering to clear the family name if she returns 'misplaced documents.' She understands he planted the frame and needs the originals destroyed. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Felix maps the route to the harbor master: the observatory gate, the customs house, the pier watch. Each checkpoint is staffed by men loyal to Corven. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic of risk.

chapters.title: An Ally in the Tower
chapters.summary: Observatory keeper Maren Ostrow, who suspects the sabotage, offers Felix a hiding place inside the clock case itself. Their alliance forms over shared loneliness. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: cautious trust.

chapters.title: The Mother Who Kept Books
chapters.summary: Felix finally tells her mother everything. Instead of collapsing, her mother produces decades of household ledgers that contradict the forged manifest. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — the mother's precision becomes armor.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Gate
chapters.summary: Night one. Felix carries the letter sewn into her coat lining through the observatory gate, where Voss searches apprentices at random. A staged mechanical failure buys her the distraction. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: heart-pounding luck.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Voss reports his suspicions to Corven; a warrant is drawn for the 'apprentice boy.' Felix learns her disguise now makes her both invisible and hunted. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the hunter's patience, unsettlingly sympathetic.

chapters.title: The Customs House Trap
chapters.summary: Corven seals the customs house for an 'audit,' trapping the documents' only other copy. Maren volunteers to create a diversion at the tower, risking her post. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered without being asked.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Audit
chapters.summary: Felix walks into the customs house posing as a courier for Corven himself, using his own seal impression copied from wax. The forgery works — barely. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: audacity riding on a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bench
chapters.summary: Tadao, terrified, tells Corven where Felix will be. Consumed by guilt, he then slips her a warning note through the workshop shutter. POV: Tadao. Emotional beat: betrayal and redemption in a single breath.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Warrens
chapters.summary: Felix flees through the dockside alleys as Voss's men sweep the district. She hides in a chandler's loft among nets, holding the letter against her heartbeat. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: raw fear transmuted into stubbornness.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Pier Watch
chapters.summary: Dawn approaches. At the pier, the watch demands papers from everyone boarding. Maren arrives with the observatory's official time-synchronization order — legitimate reason for a clockmaker to board. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: friendship tested under a lantern's glare.

chapters.title: The Manifest Sails
chapters.summary: Corven orders the ship searched, believing the letter is aboard. It sails empty-handed while Felix watches from the crowd, the real letter still against her ribs. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: triumph laced with exhaustion.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Clock Room
chapters.summary: Corven corners Felix in the observatory, alone, demanding the letter. She stalls him until the master clock strikes — and Voss, arriving, hears enough to realize whom he has truly served. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the climax — truth spoken aloud in a room built for accuracy.

chapters.title: The Harbor Master's Office
chapters.summary: Before witnesses, Felix presents the letter, the manifest, and her mother's ledgers. Voss, choosing the record over his patron, corroborates. Corven is taken into custody. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: justice as quiet procedure, not spectacle.

chapters.title: Names on the Ledger
chapters.summary: Fallout: the family name is bruised but cleared. Felix reveals herself as a woman to the guild, expecting ruin — and instead finds Maren and the harbor master vouching for her work. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: vulnerability answered by unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Setting the Clock Right
chapters.summary: Months later, Felix repairs the master clock properly, her own name entered in the observatory's log. Her father's letter is archived, not burned — memory kept whole. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: resolution — she inherits the truth along with the trade, and winds it forward.
